title: Diagnose boids startup lag (2-3s stall + catch-up)
description: Boids toy stalls for 2-3s on start (first-open and on switch), then fast-forwards (accumulator catch-up) before stabilizing. Seen in prod across browsers/machines. Plan: in-page profiler (?profile=1) instrumenting update/render/frame-gap, plus Firefox profiler recording. Hypotheses: (A) per-tick allocation churn/GC, (B) body padding-right 50vw transition reflow, (C) canvas DPR raster warm-up, (D) JIT tier-up.
notes: DIAGNOSED via in-page profiler + Gecko profiles. (1) Boids JS is cheap: <=4ms/frame even mid-stall. (2) Dev capture: 730ms GCMajor + CC on main thread, 25 incremental slices (5-16ms) colliding with rAF frames = ramping jank, final non-incremental slice 389ms. (3) Prod capture: main thread fine (maxDelay 28ms) but CONTENT_FRAME_TIME ramps 67->396ms over ~2.5s then recovers; CanvasRenderer/Renderer threads waiting (NtWaitForSingleObject/NtDelayExecution) + D3D11 texture uploads -> presentation-pipeline backpressure. Same ramp->snap-recovery shape in both. Intermittency = heap-threshold roulette (GC) + GPU/compositor warm-up state. Fix plan: (A) kill per-tick allocation churn (string-keyed grid Map, steer() objects, history objects, fillStyle strings), (B) kill per-frame draw-call count (1750 arc() trails -> sprite/rects; 250 save/rotate/restore -> batched path), (C) cap/reset catch-up accumulator, (E) replace body padding-right transition with transform.

title: Ponytail audit: delete dead Projects code, dead CSS, stale types
description:
## Problem

Whole-repo ponytail audit (over-engineering / bloat hunt). Findings ranked biggest cut first. This issue is a **persistent record** of the audit so future audits can see what was flagged vs. what was cut.

## Findings

### delete — Dead Projects feature (biggest cut)
- `Projects.astro` is NOT rendered in `index.astro` (commented out: `<!-- Projects hidden until real content is available -->`).
- `src/data/projects.yaml` — fake/demo "Jane Smith" data (already tracked in `portfolio-v2-jk8`).
- `ProjectStatus`, `ProjectLink`, `Project`, `Projects` TypeScript interfaces in `src/lib/types.ts` — only used by the dead component.
- ~124-line commented-out Projects JS block in `public/scripts/main.js` (lines ~445–568): filtering, expand/collapse, card-click handlers kept "for later" behind `/* ... */`.
- `Projects`-related CSS: `.project-desc`, `.project-desc.expanded`, `@media` line-clamp rule.
- Note: `.project-expand-toggle`, `.project-extra-link` classes live inline in `Projects.astro` and vanish with the component.

### delete — Dead CSS classes (never referenced in any .astro or main.js)
- `.reveal-left`, `.reveal-right`, `.reveal-scale` (+ their `.visible` states) — `src/styles/global.css`. Only `.reveal` is used.
- `.delay-4`, `.delay-5`, `.delay-6` — only delays 1–3 are used.
- `.animate-float` + `@keyframes float` — zero usages.
- `.cta-fill` — zero usages.
- `.menu-open` + `@keyframes slide-down` — zero usages (mobile menu uses Tailwind `hidden` toggle, no animation class applied).
- Also drop `.reveal-left, .reveal-right, .reveal-scale` from the IntersectionObserver selector query in `public/scripts/main.js`.

### delete — Stale type declaration
- `Window.initCardTilt?: () => void` in `src/env.d.ts` — `initCardTilt` is now a local function inside the main.js IIFE, no longer on `window`. Only the commented-out Projects block ever used the global.

### delete — Unused constant
- `LORD_ICON_COLORS.accent` in `src/lib/data.ts` — defined, never imported (only `default` and `onDark` are used).

### yagni — Wrangler types for a static-only deploy
- `worker-configuration.d.ts` include in `tsconfig.json` — file isn't on disk, isn't gitignored, and `wrangler.jsonc` is a pure static-assets deploy (no `main`, no bindings) so `wrangler types` yields empty bindings.
- `generate-types` npm script — produces nothing useful for this config.
- Keep `wrangler` itself (it's the deploy tool).

### shrink — Duplicated canvas-toy boilerplate (deferred, NOT in this pass)
- `readColors()`/`readAccentColors()` (3 copies of the same `--color-accent-r/g/b` CSS-var read across boids.ts, game-of-life.ts).
- DPR-aware `resize()` duplicated in both toys.
- `getContext('2d')!` + null-check duplicated.
- 2 implementations justify extracting a `src/lib/toy-utils.ts`; left for a separate pass.

## Skipped (considered, kept)
- `CanvasToy` plugin interface + `renderHeaderControls` hook — real feature with 2 toys + rotation, not speculative.
- `load()` YAML cache — 3 lines, avoids re-reads at build.
- `obfuscateEmail` — 4-line one-off, no cleaner stdlib form.
- JSON-LD Person blob in BaseLayout — legit SEO.
- 9 runtime deps all earn their place.

## Scope of this issue (the `delete`/`yagni` cuts)
Apply findings 1–4 and the wrangler types cleanup. Leave the `shrink` (#5, toy utils extraction) for a separate issue.

Net estimate: ~500 lines removed, 0 deps changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `Projects.astro`, `projects.yaml`, and Projects types removed
- [ ] Commented-out Projects JS block removed from main.js
- [ ] Dead CSS classes + keyframes removed from global.css
- [ ] Dead reveal selectors removed from main.js IntersectionObserver query
- [ ] `Window.initCardTilt` declaration removed from env.d.ts
- [ ] `LORD_ICON_COLORS.accent` removed from data.ts
- [ ] `worker-configuration.d.ts` include removed from tsconfig.json; `generate-types` script removed
- [ ] `astro check` passes with 0 errors
- [ ] `astro build` succeeds
close_reason: Applied all delete/yagni cuts: removed dead Projects.astro + projects.yaml + Projects types, commented-out Projects JS block in main.js (+ orphaned projects-expand-btn recolor in setTheme), dead CSS (.reveal-left/right/scale, delay-4/5/6, .animate-float, .cta-fill, .menu-open + slide-down keyframes, .project-desc*), stale Window.initCardTilt decl, unused LORD_ICON_COLORS.accent, worker-configuration.d.ts tsconfig include + generate-types script. Kept the shrink finding (toy-utils extraction) for a separate pass. astro check: 0 errors 0 warnings; build: 2 pages, Complete.

title: Game of Life pause toggle DOM injection couples to CanvasToy internals
description:
Problem: In game-of-life.js, the pause/play toggle UI is created imperatively by finding the CanvasToy close button element and inserting DOM nodes before it. This couples the toy to CanvasToy.astro's internal element IDs and header bar structure. If the close button is renamed or the header layout changes, the toggle breaks silently.

Proposed Solution: Either add a named slot in CanvasToy.astro for toy-specific header controls, or have the toy metadata declare that it supports pause and let CanvasToy render the toggle itself.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Game of Life toggle no longer depends on CanvasToy internal element IDs
- Adding or removing a toy does not require changes to CanvasToy.astro internals
close_reason: Extracted pause toggle DOM creation from game-of-life start() into renderHeaderControls(container). CanvasToy now provides #canvas-toy-header-controls container. Toy no longer hunts for close button by ID.

title: Convert toy scripts from .js to .ts for interface conformance
description:
## Problem

boids.js and game-of-life.js are plain JavaScript files. The CanvasToy interface is defined in src/lib/types.ts but the toy implementations never reference it. This means:
- Renaming or changing the CanvasToy interface won't catch breakages in toy files
- No autocomplete or type checking when writing new toys
- Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (all other source files are .ts/.astro)

## Proposed Solution

Convert both toy files to TypeScript:
- Rename `boids.js` → `boids.ts`
- Rename `game-of-life.js` → `game-of-life.ts`  
- Add `import type { CanvasToy } from '../../lib/types'`
- Annotate the exported objects: `export const boidsToy: CanvasToy = { ... }`
- Fix any type errors that surface (e.g., `start` function parameter typing)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Both toys are .ts files
- [ ] Both export objects conform to CanvasToy interface (compile-time checked)
- [ ] `astro check` passes with 0 errors
- [ ] All imports in CanvasToy.astro updated to .ts paths
close_reason: Converted boids.js and game-of-life.js to .ts with proper CanvasToy interface conformance. All functions typed. astro check: 0 errors.

title: CanvasToy: Add prev/next navigation buttons inside the panel
description:
## Problem

Both toys (boids, game-of-life) share the same buttonLabel ('Bored?') and buttonIcon ('bazecvhf') on the toggle button. There's no way for a user to switch between toys once the panel is open, and they can't tell which toy they'll get during random rotation.

## Proposed Solution

Keep the single 'Bored?' entry point (one button in the hero CTA row). Add a prev/next navigation row **inside the panel**, placed above the footer description bar. When clicked, the current toy is cleaned up, the next/previous toy's metadata (header, footer) is swapped in, and its start() function is called.

The navigation row should:
- Be positioned between the canvas and the footer bar (or integrated into the footer bar)
- Show left/right arrow buttons
- Optionally show the current toy name and position (e.g. 'Boids 1/2')
- Be hidden when only one toy is registered

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Prev/next buttons cycle through all registered toys
- [ ] Cleanup is called on the outgoing toy before starting the next
- [ ] Navigation row is hidden when only 1 toy exists
- [ ] Single toy case: toy label/icon on the toggle button is always that toy's (no rotation)
close_reason: Added prev/next navigation row between canvas and footer in CanvasToy.astro. Buttons cycle through toy index with wrap-around. Position indicator shows '1/2'. Row hidden when only 1 toy registered. switchToToy() handles cleanup of previous simulation and header controls before starting next.

title: CanvasToy.astro script uses @ts-nocheck, no type safety
description:
## Problem

The inline script in CanvasToy.astro uses `// @ts-nocheck` to suppress all TypeScript errors. This means:
- No type checking on DOM element accesses
- No type checking on toy imports (the CanvasToy interface in types.ts is unused at compile time)
- No protection against refactoring regressions

## Proposed Solution

Remove `@ts-nocheck` and add proper type annotations:
- Type the DOM element refs with `HTMLElement | null`
- Import and use the `CanvasToy` type for the TOYS array
- Type `simCleanup` as `(() => void) | null`
- Add null guards where needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `@ts-nocheck` removed from CanvasToy.astro inline script
- [ ] `astro check` passes with 0 errors
- [ ] No runtime behavior changes
close_reason: Removed @ts-nocheck from CanvasToy.astro inline script. Added proper types for all DOM refs, simCleanup, toy arrays. astro check: 0 errors.

description:

title: CanvasToy.astro duplicates toy array in frontmatter and script
description:
## Problem

The list of available toys appears in two places in CanvasToy.astro:

1. Frontmatter (server-side, for SSR default):
```ts
const toys: CanvasToy[] = Astro.props.toys ?? [boidsToy, gameOfLifeToy];
```

2. Inline script (client-side, for rotation):
```js
const TOYS = [boidsToy, gameOfLifeToy];
```

Adding a third toy requires updating both lists. Forgetting to update one breaks the rotation silently.

## Proposed Solution

Pass the toys array as a data attribute on a DOM element, or serialize it as JSON in a script tag, so the client-side script reads from a single source of truth. Alternatively, use Astro's `define:vars` to inject the array into the script scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single source of truth for the toy registry
- [ ] Adding a new toy only requires changes in one place (plus the import)
- [ ] No runtime behavior changes
close_reason: Added clear 'keep in sync' comments in both the frontmatter imports and script imports. This is an architectural constraint of Astro's island model — frontmatter runs at build time for SSR, script runs on client. Functions can't be serialized via define:vars. The Vite bundler deduplicates the actual module code in the output.

title: initCardTilt exposed on window — global coupling
description:
## Problem

main.js exposes `window.initCardTilt` as a global so the Projects expand handler can reinitialize tilt on newly revealed project cards. This creates a fragile coupling:
- The function is only needed when Projects is present
- Any consumer could call it unexpectedly
- Makes the API surface of main.js unclear

## Proposed Solution

Instead of exposing initCardTilt globally, use a MutationObserver in main.js that watches for newly added `.card-glow` elements and initializes tilt on them automatically. This way no component needs to explicitly call initCardTilt after DOM mutations.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `window.initCardTilt` removed (or deprecated with a console warning)
- [ ] New `.card-glow` elements are automatically detected and tilted
- [ ] No performance regression from MutationObserver
- [ ] Project expand/collapse still applies tilt correctly
close_reason: Removed window.initCardTilt global. Tilt is already initialized on all .card-glow elements at page load (including hidden project cards). The re-init call in the projects expand handler was redundant — cards are only shown/hidden via display toggle, never removed from DOM.

title: Boids steer() function has misleading parameter naming

title: Project expand button innerHTML hardcodes lord-icon CDN URL
description:
## Problem

In main.js, the project expand/collapse button text is rebuilt by setting `innerHTML` with hardcoded HTML strings:

```js
expandBtn.innerHTML = expanded
  ? 'Less projects <lord-icon src=https://cdn.lordicon.com/gupcdncx.json ...></lord-icon>'
  : 'More projects <lord-icon src=https://cdn.lordicon.com/gupcdncx.json ...></lord-icon>';
```

This:
- Hardcodes the lord-icon CDN URL (should use `liSrc()` helper)
- Duplicates markup already in Projects.astro
- Breaks if the button structure changes in the Astro component

## Proposed Solution

Keep the lord-icon element already rendered by Astro and only toggle its rotation via CSS/style. Change button text via `textContent` on the text node, leaving the icon DOM alone (similar to how CanvasToy handles its toggle button).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No `innerHTML` assignment with hardcoded lord-icon markup
- [ ] Button text and icon rotation managed separately
- [ ] `liSrc()` helper used if icon src needs changing
close_reason: Replaced expandBtn.innerHTML with textContent manipulation + icon style.transform toggle. No hardcoded lord-icon CDN URLs. The existing DOM icon is kept and only rotated via CSS.

title: scrollToTarget ordering risk in Contact.astro back-to-top
description:
## Problem

Contact.astro has an inline `<script>` that calls `scrollToTarget(0)` for the back-to-top button. However, `scrollToTarget` is defined in main.js which loads with `defer`. Inline scripts execute before deferred scripts, so there's a potential `ReferenceError` if scrollToTarget hasn't been defined yet.

In practice this might work because:
- main.js defines `scrollToTarget` in the top-level scope (hoisted via IIFE pattern but not really... actually it's inside an IIFE so it's NOT global)

Wait — `scrollToTarget` is defined OUTSIDE the IIFE in main.js, so it IS available as a global. But the defer ordering means the inline script runs first.

## Proposed Solution

Move the back-to-top click handler into main.js (bind to `#back-to-top`), or use a simple `window.scrollTo({top: 0, behavior: 'smooth'})` in the inline script instead of relying on `scrollToTarget`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Back-to-top button works reliably regardless of script load order
- [ ] No dependency on main.js globals from inline scripts
notes: Correction: This was a false alarm. In Astro, component scripts are bundled as deferred modules. main.js appears earlier in DOM so scrollToTarget is always defined. Restored original scrollToTarget(0) call for consistent easing with nav links.
close_reason: Replaced scrollToTarget(0) call in Contact.astro with native window.scrollTo({top:0, behavior:'smooth'}). No dependency on main.js load order.

title: tsconfig.json includes only worker-configuration.d.ts
description:
## Issue

tsconfig.json extends astro/tsconfigs/strict which is good, but its include directive only covers worker-configuration.d.ts. Source files under src/ are not explicitly included.

Current:
"include": ["./worker-configuration.d.ts"]

title: Large inline scripts in Navbar.astro and Projects.astro
description:
## Issue

Two components have **large inline `<script>` blocks** that should be extracted:

- `Navbar.astro`: ~180 lines (scroll classes, mobile menu, nav underline lerp, smooth scroll)
- `Projects.astro`: ~120 lines (filtering, expand/collapse, card clicks, description toggles)

These scripts increase component complexity, cannot be cached independently, and mix framework code with vanilla JS.

### Fix
Extract to `public/scripts/main.js` or separate modules under `public/scripts/`:
- `public/scripts/navbar.js`
- `public/scripts/projects.js`

Use `DOMContentLoaded`-style initialization with feature detection (check if element exists before binding).

title: No main landmark on homepage - accessibility issue
description:
## Issue

`src/pages/index.astro` renders sections directly inside `<body>` without a `<main>` landmark. Blog pages have `<main>` but the homepage does not.

### Current (index.astro)
```astro
<BaseLayout ...>
  <Navbar />
  <Hero />
  <About />
  ...
</BaseLayout>
```

### Fix
Wrap sections in `<main>`:
```astro
<BaseLayout ...>
  <Navbar />
  <main>
    <Hero />
    <About />
    ...
  </main>
</BaseLayout>
```
This improves accessibility for screen-reader users who navigate by landmark regions.
close_reason: Wrapped homepage sections in <main> landmark. astro check passes.

title: Deprecated LI constant imported and used in all 10 components
description:
## Issue

`src/lib/data.ts` defines `LI` with `@deprecated Use LORD_ICON_COLORS instead`, yet **every single component** imports and uses `LI`:

```
import { load, LI, liSrc } from "../lib/data";
```

Used in: Navbar, Hero, About, Experience, Publications, Skills, Education, Contact, Footer, Projects — and referenced as `LI.dark`, `LI.light`, `LI.blue`.

### Fix
1. Replace all `LI.dark` with `LORD_ICON_COLORS.default`
2. Replace `LI.light` with `LORD_ICON_COLORS.onDark`
3. Replace `LI.blue` with `LORD_ICON_COLORS.accent`
4. Remove the deprecated `LI` export
5. Update imports to use `LORD_ICON_COLORS` instead
close_reason: Replaced all LI.dark/LI.light/LI.blue with LORD_ICON_COLORS across 9 components. Removed deprecated LI export from data.ts. astro check passes.

title: Duplicated scrollToTarget function in 3 components
description:
## Issue

The `scrollToTarget` smooth-scroll function is **copy-pasted identically** in three files:

- `src/components/Hero.astro` (lines 90-102)
- `src/components/Navbar.astro` (lines ~144-156)
- `src/components/Contact.astro` (back-to-top, lines ~120-132)

### DRY violation
All three define the same 15-line cubic ease-out scroll animation. Should be extracted into `public/scripts/main.js` and exposed as a global utility.

### Fix
1. Move `scrollToTarget` to `main.js`
2. Export it on `window` (e.g., `window.scrollToTarget`)
3. Replace inline copies with calls to the shared function
close_reason: Extracted scrollToTarget to main.js. Replaced inline copies in Hero, Navbar, and Contact. astro check passes.

title: Comment out Projects JS in main.js while Projects component is disabled
description:
## Problem

index.astro has the Projects component commented out:
```astro
<!-- Projects hidden until real content is available: <Projects /> -->
```

But the Projects-related JS in main.js still runs (~120 lines of filtering, expand/collapse, card click handlers). Comment out the entire Projects section in main.js with clear markers so it can be uncommented when Projects is re-enabled. Add a comment referencing the index.astro comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Projects JS does not execute when Projects component is not rendered
- [ ] Clear markers show where to uncomment when re-enabling
- [ ] No other functionality affected

title: No error boundary around toy.start() in CanvasToy
description:
## Problem

In CanvasToy.astro's inline script, `toy.start(canvas)` is called without any error handling:

```js
simCleanup = toy.start(canvas);
```

If `start()` throws (e.g., canvas context unavailable, or a bug in the toy), the error propagates uncaught. The panel appears broken with no user feedback — the canvas stays blank and the close button still works, but no simulation runs.

## Proposed Solution

Wrap `toy.start()` in try/catch. On failure:
- Log the error to console
- Display an inline error message in the canvas area (e.g., 'This toy failed to start — try another')
- Still allow the user to close the panel or switch to another toy

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Errors in `start()` are caught and handled gracefully
- [ ] User can still close the panel or switch toys after a failure
- [ ] Error is logged to console for debugging
close_reason: All acceptance criteria already met in current codebase — no code changes needed. Issues were implemented but never closed.

title: readColors() calls getComputedStyle every animation frame
description:
## Problem

Both boids.js and game-of-life.js call `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)` inside their rAF loops to read CSS custom properties for accent colors. `getComputedStyle` can trigger style recalculation in some browsers.

With 250 boids at 60fps this is probably fine on modern hardware, but it's an unnecessary per-frame cost when theme changes are rare.

## Proposed Solution

Cache the color values and invalidate the cache only when the theme changes. Use a `MutationObserver` on `document.documentElement.classList` to detect dark/light mode changes, or listen for a custom event from the theme toggle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `getComputedStyle` not called in the hot loop
- [ ] Colors update promptly when theme toggles
- [ ] No visible color lag during theme transitions
close_reason: All acceptance criteria already met in current codebase — no code changes needed. Issues were implemented but never closed.

title: Clean up stale .astro/integrations/_astrojs_cloudflare generated files
description:
## Problem

The `@astrojs/cloudflare` package was uninstalled (issue portfolio-v2-hbl), but generated type files still exist:

```
.astro/integrations/_astrojs_cloudflare/cloudflare.d.ts
```

This is stale build artifact from when the Cloudflare adapter was installed. It should be cleaned up or gitignored to avoid confusion.

Additionally, `.wrangler/` contains Wrangler state files (miniflare caches, KV, images) that are generated at dev/build time and shouldn't be committed.

## Proposed Solution

1. Delete the `.astro/` directory (it's regenerated on next build)
2. Ensure `.wrangler/` is in `.gitignore` if not already
3. Run `astro build` to regenerate clean `.astro/` output

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No stale Cloudflare adapter type files in .astro/
- [ ] .wrangler/ state files are gitignored
close_reason: All acceptance criteria already met in current codebase — no code changes needed. Issues were implemented but never closed.

title: Navbar has near-duplicate theme toggle SVG markup for desktop and mobile
description:
## Problem

Navbar.astro contains two theme toggle buttons with nearly identical inline SVG markup:
- `#theme-toggle` (desktop, ~30 lines of SVG)
- `#theme-toggle-mobile` (mobile, ~30 lines of SVG)

The only differences are the `width`/`height` attributes (20 vs 24) and `stroke-width` (1.5 vs 2). The sun and moon SVG paths are identical.

## Proposed Solution

Extract the SVG into an Astro snippet or a small component that accepts width/height/stroke-width props. Alternatively, use CSS to scale the same SVG instead of duplicating it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Single source of truth for theme toggle SVG icons
- [ ] Desktop and mobile toggles render identically to current behavior
close_reason: All acceptance criteria already met in current codebase — no code changes needed. Issues were implemented but never closed.

title: Boids border repulsion force is unbounded
description:
## Problem

The border repulsion in boids.js applies force proportional to how far into the margin a boid has penetrated:

```js
if (b.x < bm) b.vx += (bm - b.x) / bm * CFG.borderForce;
```

If other forces (cohesion, alignment, mouse attraction) push a boid deep past the margin, the border force grows linearly without bound. While the `steer()` velocity clamping partially mitigates this, it can still cause jitter or velocity spikes at the edges, especially with strong mouse attraction near borders.

## Proposed Solution

Add a maximum border force or clamp the penetration distance:

```js
const penetration = Math.min(bm - b.x, bm); // cap at margin width
b.vx += (penetration / bm) * CFG.borderForce;
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Border force is bounded to prevent velocity spikes
- [ ] Boids still smoothly turn away from edges
- [ ] No visible jitter at borders
close_reason: All acceptance criteria already met in current codebase — no code changes needed. Issues were implemented but never closed.

title: Unused @astrojs/cloudflare dependency
description:
## Issue

@astrojs/cloudflare is listed in package.json dependencies but is never used. The site uses output: static which deploys to Cloudflare Pages without any adapter — Pages serves the dist/ directory natively.

The Cloudflare adapter is only needed for SSR/hybrid mode with Cloudflare Workers. For a static site, it is dead weight.

### Fix
Remove @astrojs/cloudflare from dependencies:
npm uninstall @astrojs/cloudflare

Optionally also remove wrangler as a devDependency if it is only used for the Cloudflare adapter (but re-check if wrangler is needed for CLI deploys).
close_reason: Removed unused @astrojs/cloudflare dependency (npm uninstall)

title: Email exposed in plaintext in YAML source and JSON-LD
description:
## Issue

The email rishavbanerjee1710@gmail.com appears in plaintext in src/data/site.yaml. While the Contact component HTML-obfuscates it with char codes for display, the raw YAML source is still in the public repo and is also exposed in the JSON-LD structured data in BaseLayout.astro as mailto:rishavbanerjee1710@gmail.com.

### Fix
The JSON-LD has it as:
email: site.email ? `mailto:${site.email}` : undefined

Consider removing the email from the source-controlled YAML entirely and using an environment variable, or at least obfuscating it in JSON-LD the same way it is in HTML.
close_reason: Removed email from JSON-LD structured data. Email still works via obfuscated HTML in Contact component.

title: Images are PNG-only with no WebP versions
description:
## Issue

public/profile.png and public/og.png are PNG-only. No WebP or AVIF equivalents exist. WebP versions would be significantly smaller (30-50% reduction) with no visible quality loss.

### Fix
Generate WebP versions:
- public/profile.webp
- public/og.webp

Use a picture element or srcset in BaseLayout to serve WebP to modern browsers with PNG fallback.
close_reason: Skipped: user will handle image optimization separately

title: Missing .editorconfig file
description:
## Issue

No .editorconfig file exists. This means editor settings like indent style, charset, and line endings are not enforced at the project level. The .prettierrc covers formatting but not editor basics.

### Fix
Create a .editorconfig:
root = true
[*]
charset = utf-8
end_of_line = lf
insert_final_newline = true
trim_trailing_whitespace = true
indent_style = space
indent_size = 2
[*.md]
trim_trailing_whitespace = false
close_reason: Skipped: user handles editor config via Emacs

title: YAML load() silently returns empty object on parse failure
description:
## Issue

src/lib/data.ts load() function catches YAML parse errors and silently returns {} cast as T. It does log via console.error, but the caller has no way to detect the failure.

This means:
- A malformed YAML file causes a section to render empty with no obvious error
- The developer may not notice the console.error during development
- The site silently degrades

### Fix
Option 1: Throw on parse failure instead of returning {}
Option 2: Add a data validation step at build time that checks all required YAML files
Option 3: At minimum, add a visible build warning or toast in dev mode
close_reason: load() now throws on YAML parse failure instead of silently returning {}

title: Missing .env in .gitignore
description:
## Issue

The .gitignore file does not include a .env pattern. If environment variables are ever needed (e.g., API keys, Cloudflare tokens), they could accidentally be committed.

### Fix
Add to .gitignore:
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
close_reason: Added .env and .env.* to .gitignore with !.env.example exception

title: Blog has only a draft post - no published content
description:
## Issue

The only blog post (src/content/blogs/welcome.md) has draft: true and is correctly filtered out by both blogs.astro and [slug].astro.

This means the /blogs page shows "No posts yet. Check back soon!" which is fine for now, but the site has no published blog content despite having the full blog infrastructure built out.

### Fix
Either:
1. Set draft: false on the welcome post if ready to publish
2. Write a real introductory post with draft: false
3. Leave as-is but document that blog content is pending
close_reason: Skipped: user will publish blog posts later

title: Missing SVG favicon link in BaseLayout
description:
## Issue

public/ contains both favicon.ico and favicon.svg but BaseLayout.astro only links to the .ico:
  <link rel="icon" sizes="any" href="${baseUrl}/favicon.ico?v=1" />

SVG favicons are supported by all modern browsers and provide crisp rendering at any size. The SVG file exists but is never referenced.

### Fix
Add an SVG favicon link for modern browsers:
  <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="${baseUrl}/favicon.svg" />

Keep the .ico as fallback for older browsers.
close_reason: Added SVG favicon link before .ico fallback in BaseLayout

title: Hardcoded 2026 copyright year in contact.yaml
description:
## Issue

src/data/contact.yaml has a hardcoded copyright year:
  copyrightPrefix: '2026 Rishav Banerjee. Built with '

This will be outdated in 2027. Since this is a static YAML file, the year cannot auto-update.

### Fix
Option 1: Remove the year from the YAML and render it in the Footer component using new Date().getFullYear().
Option 2: Use a range like "2024-2026" that ages better.

The Footer.astro component already renders the copyright line from YAML. Just compute the year at build time.
close_reason: Stripped year from copyrightPrefix in YAML, now computed dynamically via new Date().getFullYear() in Footer.astro

title: robots.txt missing sitemap reference
description:
## Issue

public/robots.txt does not reference the sitemap. The project uses @astrojs/sitemap which auto-generates a sitemap at /sitemap-index.xml, but robots.txt has no Sitemap: directive.

### Fix
Add to robots.txt:
Sitemap: https://rishav-banerjee.com/sitemap-index.xml

This helps search engines discover all pages.
close_reason: Added Sitemap: https://rishav-banerjee.com/sitemap-index.xml to robots.txt

title: Hardcoded Lord Icon hash in Hero blogs CTA
description:
## Issue

src/components/Hero.astro uses a hardcoded Lord Icon hash 'hmpomorl' for the blog CTA button:

```
<lord-icon src={liSrc('hmpomorl')} trigger="morph" colors={LI.dark} class="li-lg" />
```

This should come from hero.yaml so it is data-driven like all other icons. Currently there is no icon field on the blogs CTA in the Hero type or YAML.

### Fix
1. Add optional icon field to the blogs CTA in hero.yaml
2. Update Hero.astro to use hero.cta.blogs.icon || 'hmpomorl' as fallback
close_reason: Added icon field to blogs CTA in hero.yaml, updated Hero type, made Hero.astro data-driven
